PART 0

Overview

What the platform is, how it is built, and how to read this guide.

0.1The platform at a glance

CFA Learning Hub by Karan Sir Classes is a learning-management system for the CFA Level I exam. Candidates register and pay for a course, then study 56 learning modules (LMs) across 10 subjects with class videos, notes and PDFs. They test themselves with chapter quizzes, subject tests and custom quizzes, revise with spaced-repetition flashcards, and track progress. Staff author and publish content; admins run registrations, payments, people and compliance.

UI workflows

How candidates, staff and admins move through the product, screen by screen.

1.1Who uses the platform

Three audiences share one application. The menu a person sees is built from the permissions their roles carry, so a candidate never sees the staff console and an author never sees refunds.

AudienceRolesPrimary goalsHome screen
CandidatestudentPass CFA Level I: learn, practise, revise, track progress. Pay and get receipts. Control personal data./dashboard
Staffauthor, reviewerAuthor: write notes, upload videos/PDFs, write questions and flashcards. Reviewer: publish content and read progress reports./admin
Adminadmin, super_adminRun the business: courses and fees, registrations, orders and refunds, users and batches, privacy requests, audit trail. Super admin also assigns admins./admin

1.3The candidate journey

1.4Workflow C1 · Sign-in and sign-up

Candidates never create a password. A one-time code sent to their mobile proves ownership, and the same screen handles both existing and new accounts. Email OTP exists in the API for later use.

RuleValueSource
Code validity5 minutes, single useotp_ttl_seconds=300
Code requests5 per hour per mobile or emailotp_max_requests_per_hour
Wrong guesses5 per code, then a new code is requiredotp_max_attempts
Devices2 active sessions; the oldest ends when a third signs instudent_max_sessions (BR-ACC-05)
Mobile formatIndian numbers only: +91 followed by 10 digits starting 6–9MOBILE_RE

1.5Workflow C2 · Under-18 candidates and guardian consent

Under India's DPDP rules, a child's data needs a parent's verifiable consent. A candidate whose date of birth gives an age below 18 gets status pending_guardian. They can sign in and see /pending-consent but cannot register, pay or study until the guardian approves.

1.6Workflow C3 · Choosing, registering and paying

★
Why this is safe
Orders are idempotent (the same payment applied twice changes nothing), amounts are compared to the order (mismatch is flagged, never granted), and an unpaid order is reused for 30 minutes so a refresh cannot create duplicate charges.

1.7Workflow C4 · Learning

BehaviourRuleWhere enforced
Resource completionA video or PDF counts as done at ≥ 90% watched (merged watched intervals, so skipping back does not double count)progress/service.py COMPLETION_THRESHOLD
Mark as learnedAllowed any time; can be undone for 24 hourslm_progress.learned_undo_until

1.8Workflow C5 · Tests and quizzes

TestQuestionsTimingAdvisory pass markStarted from
Chapter quiz10 (min 3 available)90 s per question80%LM view → Chapter quiz
Subject (master) test5090 s per question75%Custom Quiz → Subject tests
Custom quizYour choiceOptional timernoneCustom Quiz: subjects, chapters, difficulty (E/M/H), conceptual / numerical, practice or assessment
★
Answer keys stay on the server
In assessment mode the correct answer and explanation are not sent to the browser until that question is submitted. The attempt stores a snapshot of each question, so later edits by staff never change a past result.

1.9Workflow C6 · Flashcards and spaced repetition

Cards are grouped into decks by subject. After flipping a card the candidate rates it Known, Needs revision or Difficult. A modified SM-2 scheduler sets the next due date.

RatingEffect
KnownInterval 1 d → 3 d → previous × ease
Needs revisionInterval × 1.2, ease − 0.15
DifficultBack to 1 day, ease − 0.2, counts a lapse
FloorEase never below 1.3

1.10Workflow C7 · Search, bookmarks, orders and profile

  • Search (/search?q=) finds learning modules (by title or summary) and published notes (PostgreSQL full-text search). Results outside the candidate's subjects show the title but no text snippet.
  • Bookmarks save a note, a video position or an LM with an optional note (500 characters).
  • Devices lists active sessions with a device label such as “Chrome on Windows”; ending one revokes its refresh token immediately.

1.11Staff and admin workflows

Workflow S0 · Signing in to the console

Staff sign in at /staff/login with email and password, then a six-digit authenticator code. First-time staff are walked through enrolling an authenticator app. Outside local development, MFA is mandatory and the server refuses to start without it.

Workflow S1 · Content and question lifecycle

i
Upload safety
Videos and PDFs are accepted only for allowed MIME types; PDFs must start with the %PDF signature; size is capped at 500 MB; licensed third-party material needs a licence reference. An antivirus scan step is planned before publish (not yet implemented).

2.2Technical architecture: a modular monolith

The API is one deployable service organised into modules. Each module owns its models, service functions and router. Modules talk through service calls and domain events, never by reaching into each other's tables, which keeps a later split into separate services possible without a rewrite (the payments module is already written to be replaceable by an external service).

ModuleOwns tablesResponsibility
authotp_challenges, sessionsOTP, staff login, TOTP, session rotation
usersusers, user_roles, guardiansIdentity records
catalog · content · mediasubjects, learning_modules, topics, los · content_* · resourcesWhat there is to learn, versioned, with files
learning · progresslm_progress, resource_progress, revision_logs, eoc_entries, bookmarksReading content, tracking progress, search
qbankquestions, test_attempts, attempt_itemsQuestion bank, tests, grading
flashcardsflashcards, card_reviewsCards and spaced repetition
commerce · enrolmentcourses, registrations, batches, enrolments, entitlementsSelling a course and granting access
paymentsorders, payments, payment_events, refundsGateway adapters (Razorpay, mock), webhooks, refunds
privacy · auditconsents, data_requests, audit_log, outbox, settingsDPDP compliance, tamper-evident log, events

2.4Domain events and the outbox

Payments finishing must open access, and a full refund must close it. These cross-module reactions use a small event bus. publish() writes the event to an outbox table and calls in-process subscribers inside the caller's transaction, so local consistency is immediate and atomic. A background loop then forwards pending events to an optional HTTP sink, signed with HMAC, so another team's service (CRM, analytics) can listen without touching this code.

2.5Deployment today: one container on Render

VariableStaging valuePurpose
APP_ENVstagingActivates production-style guard rails
DEMO_MODEtrue (staging only)On-screen OTP and mock gateway until SMS and Razorpay are connected; production refuses to start with it
COOKIE_SECURE · STAFF_MFA_REQUIREDtrue · trueMandatory outside local/test; server asserts at start-up
PAYMENT_PROVIDERmock → razorpaySelects gateway adapter
SECRET_KEYgenerated by RenderSigns every JWT and keyed hash (min 32 chars)
DATABASE_URLfrom Render PostgresAuto-rewritten to the asyncpg driver
SEED_ON_START · SEED_STAFF_PASSWORDtrue · promptedIdempotent demo catalogue and four staff accounts
!
Free-plan limits to know
Render's free web service sleeps after 15 minutes idle (first request takes about a minute), has no persistent disk (uploaded PDFs vanish on redeploy) and its free Postgres expires after 30 days. Move to a paid plan, or to S3 for uploads, before real students sign up.

2.6Target architecture: AWS Mumbai

The infrastructure document (A-05) defines where the platform is heading once traffic and compliance needs outgrow a single container. The application code is already stateless apart from the media directory, so the move is mostly infrastructure.

2.7Quality and delivery

  • Backend tests run against a separate cfa_lms_test database with real PostgreSQL features (advisory locks, JSONB).
  • Covered: OTP and session rules, staff login and MFA, privacy and consent, payments, webhooks and refunds, learning progress, tests and flashcards.
  • Frontend: tsc --noEmit and next build must pass.
  • CI/CD design (D-02) and branching (D-03) are documented; pipeline files are not yet in the repo.

3.1API conventions

TopicConvention
Base path/api/v1. Interactive docs at /api/v1/docs exist only in local/test.
FormatJSON in and out; file upload uses multipart (POST /admin/resources).
AuthenticationHttpOnly access_token cookie (or Authorization: Bearer). See Part 5.
CSRFUnsafe methods carrying the cookie must send X-CSRF-Token equal to the csrf_token cookie. Exempt: sign-in endpoints, refresh, webhooks, guardian links.
IdempotencyPayment application and webhooks are idempotent by provider ids; unpaid order reuse for 30 min.
Paginationlimit query parameter with a hard cap (500 admin lists, 200 attempts).
TracingEvery response carries x-request-id; the same id is in logs and audit rows.
CachingCache-Control: no-store on all API responses except signed media (private, 1 h).

3.4Database design

Design rules

  • UUIDv7 primary keys everywhere except two append-only logs (audit_log, outbox) which use identity integers to give a total order.
  • JSONB only for genuinely flexible payloads: note bodies, question options, attempt snapshots, watched intervals, audit changes.
  • Referential actions: user-owned rows CASCADE on delete (erasure is simple); orders and courses are RESTRICT so financial history cannot be orphaned.
  • Money is stored as integer paise, never floats. GST-inclusive fee on the course.
  • Secrets are stored only as hashes (OTP, refresh token, password) or, for TOTP, as base32 bytes awaiting KMS envelope encryption.
  • Constraints do the policing: partial unique index for one open registration per user and course; unique (provider, event_id) for webhook replay; unique per-day revision count.

PART 5

Authentication & security

Every credential, token and control that protects candidates, staff and money.

5.1Defence in depth

5.2Catalogue of authentication mechanisms

#MechanismUsed byHow it worksKey parameters
1Mobile OTPCandidates6-digit random code; stored as sha256(challenge_id:code); destination stored only as a keyed HMAC5 min TTL · 5 requests/h · 5 guesses · single use
2Email OTPCandidates (API-ready)Same engine, channel = emailsame
3Password + TOTPStaffArgon2id password, then RFC 6238 authenticator code (±1 step window)5 fails → 15 min lock · TOTP mandatory outside dev
4Signup tokenNew candidatesJWT purpose=signup proves the verified mobile until the form is submitted20 min
5MFA step-up tokenStaffJWT purpose=mfa carries the user between password and TOTP5 min
6Access tokenEveryone signed inHS256 JWT in HttpOnly cookie access_token; carries sub, session id, roles; session row re-checked on every call15 min
7Refresh tokenEveryone signed inOpaque random token, only its sha256 stored; rotated on every use; reuse of an old one revokes the sessionStudent 30 d · staff 12 h
8CSRF tokenBrowser writesDouble-submit: cookie csrf_token must equal header X-CSRF-Tokenper session
9Guardian consentParents of minorsJWT link (purpose=guardian) plus the guardian's own OTPlink 7 d · OTP 5 min
10Signed media URLVideo / PDF viewersJWT purpose=media bound to resource and user2 h
11Checkout signaturePaymentsGateway signature verified server-side, then the payment is fetched from the gatewayper payment
12Webhook HMACGateway → APIRazorpay signature on raw body; event id deduplicatedper event
13Event-sink HMACAPI → partner servicex-event-signature = HMAC-SHA256 of body with the secret keyper event
★
Purpose-bound tokens
All JWTs share one signing key but carry a pur claim (access, signup, mfa, guardian, media). decode_token(token, purpose) rejects a token whose purpose differs, so a media link can never be used as an access token and vice versa.

5.3Candidate sign-in sequence

5.4Sessions, cookies and refresh rotation

CookieHttpOnlyPathSameSiteSecurePurpose
access_tokenyes/Laxrequired outside devAuthenticates API calls
refresh_tokenyes/api/v1/authLaxrequired outside devOnly sent to the auth endpoints, so it is rarely exposed
csrf_tokenno (read by JS)/Laxrequired outside devEchoed in the X-CSRF-Token header
  • Immediate revocation. Because every request checks the sessions row, ending a session (logout, admin force sign-out, deactivation, erasure) takes effect on the very next call, not 15 minutes later.
  • Device limit. Students may hold 2 live sessions; signing in on a third ends the oldest (BR-ACC-05). Staff are not limited but expire in 12 h.
  • Visible to the user. Profile → Signed-in devices lists each session with device label and last seen.

5.5Authorisation

  • RBAC, deny by default. Roles map to permissions in one file; endpoints declare require('perm'). A role not listed grants nothing.
  • Entitlements are the second gate for content: an LM, note, video, quiz or flashcard in a subject opens only when an active entitlement exists (granted by registration, batch or manual grant). Staff preview everything.
  • Ownership checks. Attempts, orders, bookmarks, sessions and data exports are always filtered by the caller's user id; a wrong id returns 404, not 403, so ids cannot be probed.
  • Separation of duties. Authors cannot publish; reviewers cannot edit commerce; only super admins assign admin roles.

5.6How credentials are stored

SecretStored asNotes
Staff passwordArgon2id · time 3 · memory 64 MiB · parallelism 2argon2-cffi; verify is constant-time; generic error for unknown user and wrong password
OTP codesha256(challenge_id : code)Plain code exists only in the SMS
OTP destinationHMAC-SHA256 keyed with SECRET_KEYRate-limit counts without storing the number
Refresh tokensha256 of 256-bit random valueDatabase leak cannot be replayed
TOTP secretbase32 bytes in users.totp_secretNever returned by the API; KMS envelope encryption is a TODO for the cloud move
JWT signing keySECRET_KEY environment variable, ≥ 32 charsStart-up refuses the default key outside dev
Gateway secretsEnvironment variables (Secrets Manager in target)Never logged or stored in the database

5.7Integrity, audit and privacy controls

  • Hash-chained audit log. Each row stores hash = SHA-256(previous hash + canonical row). GET /admin/audit/verify recomputes the chain; any edited or deleted row breaks every later hash. Writes are serialised with an advisory lock.
  • What is audited. Sign-in and failures, lockouts, MFA enrolment, session revocation, user and role changes, orders, payments, refunds, mismatches, content and question publishing, resource uploads, consents, data requests and erasure.
  • Consent ledger. Append-only rows with notice version, actor (self or guardian), method, IP and user agent.
  • Erasure. Personal fields are overwritten and progress rows deleted; orders are kept as business records with the user pseudonymised.
  • Start-up guard rails. Outside local/test the server refuses to run unless COOKIE_SECURE and STAFF_MFA_REQUIRED are on and SECRET_KEY is changed; DEMO_MODE and on-screen OTP are blocked in production.

5.8Threats and the controls that answer them
